$comment:
AI-native `decision` object reader corpus, v0 -- the typed, fail-closed view of the shared decision object the AI-native wire returns (POST /tool-call, POST /stream/open; contract AI_NATIVE_V1_CONTRACT.md, additive-only).

WHAT THIS CORPUS PINS. Both SDKs expose the SERVER-DERIVED `fragment_tags[]`, the value-free attribution trace `parts[]`, and the chain pointers `decision_id` / `receipt_event_id` / `ledgered` through one reader with one refusal code. The reader never defaults a field the wire did not send: an absent `fragment_tags` is a malformed decision, not an empty tag set, because a defaulted [] would claim 'no tags released' for a plane that never said so (the same class of silent no-op the request side is being held back to avoid).

THE MUTANTS THIS CORPUS EXISTS TO KILL. (1) A reader that defaults absent members and turns a malformed object into a clean-looking view. (2) A tag or a partial's tag that smuggles a value onto the surface (INV-6). (3) A cross-language type gap -- a boolean accepted as an integer in one SDK and refused in the other. (4) Passing the whole response body where the `decision` member was expected and getting an empty view instead of an error.

Each invalid vector pins the refusal code AND a message fragment so both SDKs name the same member in the same words.
